deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is the draft opening of Riemann's 1861 paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). It continues Dirichlet's posthumous memoir of 1860. The page sets up kinematic variables; the following page derives the equations of motion.

Preamble. A homogeneous self-gravitating fluid ellipsoid is considered. Dirichlet was 'not granted to pursue his beautiful discovery in detail'. The present work is meant as a contribution to that further development.

Setup and notation.
- a, b, c are the semi-axes at time t; a0, b0, c0 are their initial values.
- (x, y, z) is the position of a fluid element at time t in fixed axes; (x0, y0, z0) is its initial position.
- At t = 0 the ellipsoid's axes coincide with the coordinate axes.
- Write X0 = (x0/a0, y0/b0, z0/c0)^T.

Step 1: Dirichlet's ansatz, eq. (1). The motion is taken to be linear and homogeneous in the initial data: x = M X0. Here M is the 3x3 matrix with rows (l, m, n), (l', m', n'), (l'', m'', n''). (Implicit, mine: from x(0) = x0 one gets M(0) = diag(a0, b0, c0).)

Step 2: body-axis coordinates, eq. (2). Let (xi, eta, zeta) be coordinates in the frame of the ellipsoid's principal axes at time t. Then (xi, eta, zeta)^T = A x, where A has rows (alpha, beta, gamma), (alpha', beta', gamma'), (alpha'', beta'', gamma''). Its entries are direction cosines, e.g. alpha = cos(xi, x), beta = cos(xi, y). They satisfy six conditions, expressed by eq. (3): xi^2 + eta^2 + zeta^2 = x^2 + y^2 + z^2 identically, i.e. A^T A = I.

Step 3: material surface, eq. (4). The surface always consists of the same particles. Hence xi^2/a^2 + eta^2/b^2 + zeta^2/c^2 = x0^2/a0^2 + y0^2/b0^2 + z0^2/c0^2.
- Strictly, both sides are quadratic forms in X0. Equality on the bounding surface (level 1) extends to all X0 by homogeneity. (This remark is mine.)
- So with D = diag(a, b, c), the matrix B := D^{-1} A M satisfies B^T B = I.
- This gives eq. (5): (xi/a, eta/b, zeta/c)^T = B X0. B has rows (alpha1, beta1, gamma1), (alpha1', ...), (alpha1'', ...).
- Riemann states that the alpha1, ... are again the coefficients of an orthogonal transformation. They are the direction cosines between the ellipsoid's axes and a second moving frame (xi1, eta1, zeta1).

Step 4: decomposition, eq. (6). Eliminating via (2) and (5) gives x = A^T D B X0, i.e. M = A^T diag(a, b, c) B. Componentwise:
- l = a alpha alpha1 + b alpha' alpha1' + c alpha'' alpha1''
- m = a alpha beta1 + b alpha' beta1' + c alpha'' beta1''
- l' = a beta alpha1 + b beta' alpha1' + c beta'' alpha1''
- and so on.

Thus the nine Dirichlet coefficients are expressed by the three axes a, b, c and the orientations of two moving orthogonal frames (3 + 3 + 3 parameters).

Step 5: duality remark. Interchanging the two coordinate systems (A <-> B) replaces M by M^T. So l, m', n'' are unchanged while the off-diagonal pairs (l' with m, etc.) are exchanged. This is the germ of Riemann's later observation that each motion has an 'adjoint' motion (Dedekind's reciprocity).

Step 6: plan. The final lines announce deriving, from Dirichlet's fundamental equations, the differential equations for the principal axes and for the motion of the two frames. The next page carries this out with angular velocities p, q, r and p1, q1, r1.
errors: No mathematical error. The derivation of (6) from (2) and (5) is correct and so is the symmetry remark.

Eq. (4) is stated only for the bounding surface. Concluding that the full quadratic forms coincide, and hence that B is orthogonal, needs the homogeneity remark (or the fact that all similar interior ellipsoidal shells are material). Riemann leaves this implicit.
Writing x = A^T D B X0 tacitly uses A^{-1} = A^T, which follows from (3).

results.what: Dirichlet's linear ansatz x = M X0 for motions of a homogeneous self-gravitating fluid ellipsoid
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1857 lecture; posthumous memoir ed. Dedekind, 1860)

results.what: Factorisation of the deformation matrix M = A^T diag(a,b,c) B into two rotations and the semi-axes, eq. (6)
results.modern_name: Singular value decomposition / polar decomposition of the deformation gradient applied to Riemann ellipsoids
results.usually_credited_to: As a general matrix theorem: Beltrami (1873), Jordan (1874); in this fluid-dynamics use: Riemann (1861 paper)

results.what: Interchanging the two frames transposes M (diagonal entries fixed, off-diagonal entries swapped)
results.modern_name: Adjoint motions / Dedekind's reciprocity theorem (M <-> M^T)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the opening of Riemann's published 1861 ellipsoid paper. The decomposition (6) and the two-frame description appear there and are well known (e.g. Chandrasekhar, Ellipsoidal Figures of Equilibrium). Only minor drafting variants are new.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; th1,th2,a,b,c=symbols('th1 th2 a b c'); A=rot_axis3(th1); B=rot_axis1(th2); D=diag(a,b,c); M=A.T*D*B; simplify(M[0,0]-(a*A[0,0]*B[0,0]+b*A[1,0]*B[1,0]+c*A[2,0]*B[2,0]))==0
checkable.asserts: l = a*alpha*alpha1 + b*alpha'*alpha1' + c*alpha''*alpha1'' for M = A^T D B
the formulas for m and l' in eq. (6)
with M = A^T D B, the surface condition (4) holds identically in X0
swapping the roles of the two frames (A <-> B) gives M^T: l, m', n'' fixed, off-diagonal entries exchanged

transcription_corrections: The direction cosines should read alpha = cos(xi,x), beta = cos(xi,y) (first row of A), not 'beta = cos eta y'.
The Dirichlet line is better read as 'Es ist ihm selbst aber nicht vergönnt gewesen, seine schöne Entdeckung im Einzelnen zu verfolgen' (referring to Dirichlet, d. 1859).
'Diese bezeichnet man' should be 'Bezeichnet man ... die Coefficienten ... durch alpha1, beta1, gamma1, ...'.

'Gedächtniß' in the line about interchanging the coordinate systems is almost certainly a misreading. Context requires something like 'in den Systemen der Größen alpha, beta, gamma und alpha1, beta1, gamma1 ...'. The sense is that l, m', n'' stay unchanged while l', l'' etc. are interchanged with m, n.
Title is likely 'Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen homogenen Ellipsoids' (the struck word before it is uncertain).
